name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest merged PR first. This gives us production-grade feedback without risk—we see real gaps before trusting the tool. The trade-off is delayed visibility into issues, but safety outweighs speed here.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode on merged PRs trains reviewers to ignore real issues because the tool’s noise becomes normal—we risk missing the edge cases that break open PRs. Instead, run PR-Agent in shadow mode on open PRs first, then flip to merged PRs only after we’ve tuned the signal-to-noise ratio. Settle it by measuring the false-positive rate in shadow mode for one sprint and comparing the review quality before and after.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *both* open and merged PRs from day one—this catches edge cases early while still protecting merged PRs from noise. The cost is double the compute, but the benefit is a single, consistent review process that avoids later rework.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on open PRs first, then expand to merged PRs after tuning. This catches edge cases early without risking missed issues in open PRs. The trade-off is extra compute upfront, but it prevents rework and noise habituation later.
